25 Free Resources for Managing Conflict in Relationships

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 9:57
Instaread

Conflict is a normal part of any relationship, but how couples handle it can make the difference between growing closer and slowly pulling apart. Healthy conflict isn’t about never arguing or always agreeing. It’s about learning how to disagree without attacking, shutting down, or losing sight of the fact that you’re on the same team. The 25 free resources for conflict in relationships below include worksheets, assessments, videos, interactive tools, research-based exercises, and guides.

1. Couples Coach | App

The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs’ Couples Coach is a free app designed to help couples strengthen their relationships and improve communication. It includes guided exercises, relationship assessments, and practical tools for managing conflict, increasing connection, and working through common relationship challenges. Although developed by the VA, Couples Coach is available for anyone to use.

2. Effective Communication Skills: Resolving Conflicts | USU

Advertisement
Privacy Settings

Utah State University’s Effective Communication Skills: Resolving Conflicts guide offers practical strategies for handling disagreements more constructively. It covers skills such as active listening, using “I” statements, understanding different communication styles, taking breaks when emotions become overwhelming, and working together to solve problems. The guide can help you communicate more effectively while preventing everyday disagreements from escalating.

3. When Emotions Take Over: Learning to P.A.U.S.E. Before You React | USU

Utah State University’s P.A.U.S.E. strategy offers a practical way to manage strong emotions before they take over during conflict. The guide explains how emotional and physiological reactions can make productive communication difficult and provides a step-by-step approach for slowing down, regulating your response, and returning to the conversation more calmly and intentionally.

4. Conflict Resolution – Healthy Relationships – Love Is Respect

Love Is Respect’s Conflict Resolution guide explains how to handle disagreements in healthy, respectful ways. It covers communication, compromise, boundaries, and finding solutions that work for both people while emphasizing that conflict should never involve threats, control, or abuse. The guide can also help you recognize the difference between normal relationship conflict and unhealthy behavior.

5. How to Resolve Conflicts

The American Psychological Association’s How to Resolve Conflicts guide provides a simple framework for working through disagreements constructively. It introduces the IDEAL approach, which involves identifying the problem and feelings involved, exploring possible solutions, evaluating your options, acting on a solution, and learning from the outcome. The framework can be used to approach conflict more thoughtfully and collaboratively.

Advertisement
Privacy Settings

6. Happy Couples: How to Keep Your Relationship Healthy

The American Psychological Association’s guide to healthy relationships offers research-based strategies for building and maintaining a strong partnership. It covers healthy communication, handling disagreements constructively, maintaining emotional connection, and recognizing when recurring problems may require additional support. The guide also explains how couples can approach conflict as a problem to solve together rather than a battle to win.

7. Relationship Conflict Resolution | Worksheet | Therapist Aid

Therapist Aid’s Relationship Conflict Resolution worksheet provides practical strategies for handling disagreements in healthier, more productive ways. It teaches five conflict-resolution skills, including focusing on the problem rather than the person, reflective listening, using “I” statements, taking a time-out when emotions become overwhelming, and working toward a resolution. The free worksheet can be downloaded, printed, or completed digitally.

Advertisement
Privacy Settings

8. Dealing with Conflict

Penn State Extension’s Dealing with Conflict guide offers practical strategies for handling disagreements more effectively in a variety of relationships. It covers active listening, using “I” statements, asking questions for clarification, paying attention to tone and body language, managing emotional reactions, and apologizing when appropriate. The guide also explores different conflict-management styles and how your approach can influence the outcome of a disagreement.

9. Free Conflict Resolution Worksheets for Couples

PositivePsychology.com’s Conflict Resolution Worksheets collection offers practical exercises designed to help couples work through disagreements more constructively. The worksheets explore underlying concerns, encourage active listening and perspective-taking, and help partners identify solutions that address both people’s needs. The collection also includes exercises for reflecting on past conflicts and developing healthier approaches to future disagreements.

10. Relationship Satisfaction Test (CSI-16) | Psychology.com

Psychology.com’s Relationship Satisfaction Test is a free, confidential 16-question assessment based on the validated Couples Satisfaction Index (CSI-16). It takes about four minutes and measures overall relationship satisfaction, including feelings of connection, teamwork, and whether the relationship is meeting your needs. After completing the assessment, you’ll receive a score with a plain-language explanation of what your results may mean.

11. Repair: Free Conflict Resolution & Communication Tools for Couples

Advertisement
Privacy Settings

Repair offers free, interactive tools designed to help couples communicate more effectively and work through conflict together. Its Skills section teaches evidence-inspired relationship strategies and includes short quizzes, while guided Repair Sessions walk partners through disagreements step by step. Couples explore their perspectives, emotions, triggers, accountability, and possible solutions, all directly in their browser with no account or download required.

Advertisement
Privacy Settings

12. Free Couples Communication Workbook

South Denver Therapy’s free Couples Communication Workbook is a comprehensive 58-page resource with more than 50 exercises couples can complete together. It includes a relationship assessment, communication patterns quiz, active listening tools, conflict-resolution and fair-fighting exercises, repair strategies, weekly check-ins, and activities for strengthening emotional connection. The workbook is completely free to download with no credit card required. (You must enter an email address to receive the download.)

13. Gaining Perspective on an Argument | Practice | Greater Good in Action

UC Berkeley’s Greater Good in Action offers a free 15-minute exercise designed to help couples approach disagreements from a different perspective. You’ll reflect on a recent conflict from the viewpoint of a neutral third party who wants the best for both partners. The research-based exercise can help reduce emotional distress, increase empathy, and encourage more constructive responses during future disagreements. A free printable PDF version is also available.

14. Time Out Module – Charis Institute

Regent University’s Charis Institute offers a free Time Out Module for couples whose arguments have become too heated to resolve productively. The resource includes a brief demonstration video and a downloadable worksheet to help each partner identify personal warning signs that emotions are escalating. Couples can use these signs to recognize when it’s time to pause an argument and return to the conversation when they can communicate more effectively.

Advertisement
Privacy Settings

15. TED Video: Even Healthy Couples Fight — the Difference Is How

In this TED Talk, renowned relationship researchers Drs. John and Julie Gottman explain why conflict itself isn’t necessarily a sign of an unhealthy relationship. Drawing on decades of research with couples, they explore what separates constructive disagreements from destructive ones and share strategies for approaching conflict with greater understanding, curiosity, and connection.

16. Video: Healthy vs. Harmful Conflict: Understanding the Difference – Center for Marriage and Relationships

Biola University’s Center for Marriage and Relationships offers a free video exploring the difference between healthy and harmful conflict. Chris Grace, PhD, and Alisa Grace discuss common destructive patterns such as criticism, defensiveness, contempt, and stonewalling and offer practical strategies for responding differently. The 50-minute video also covers emotional flooding, gentle ways to start difficult conversations, taking healthy time-outs, identifying the emotions beneath an argument, and repairing connection after conflict.

17. What Is Stonewalling and How to Stop

Cleveland Clinic’s guide to stonewalling explains what happens when one partner emotionally withdraws or shuts down during conflict and why this pattern can damage a relationship over time. Psychologist Susan Albers, PsyD, discusses intentional and unintentional stonewalling and offers practical strategies for changing the pattern, including recognizing when you’re shutting down, taking a purposeful time-out, communicating your needs, practicing empathy, and returning to difficult conversations when you’re ready to engage more productively.

Advertisement
Privacy Settings

18. Resources for Love, Sex, & Relationships

Mind Remake Project’s Resources for Love, Sex, & Relationships is a large collection of free tools for building healthier relationships. Resources include relationship and communication assessments, couples workbooks, worksheets, videos, guides, and interactive tools covering communication, intimacy, boundaries, attachment, conflict, and relationship satisfaction. The collection is especially useful if you want to explore several different aspects of your relationship in one place.

19. Conflict Resolution in Relationships & Couples: 5 Strategies

PositivePsychology.com’s Conflict Resolution in Relationships & Couples guide offers research-informed strategies and practical exercises for working through disagreements more constructively. It covers purposeful listening, managing strong emotions, finding win-win solutions, improving communication, and preventing unresolved issues from building resentment. The guide also includes several free exercises and worksheets couples can use to identify recurring conflicts, better understand each other’s needs, brainstorm solutions, and conduct regular relationship check-ins.

Advertisement
Privacy Settings

20. Relationship Resources | Texas Woman’s University

Texas Woman’s University’s Relationship Resources page offers a collection of practical information for building healthier relationships and communicating more effectively. It covers communication during disagreements, active listening, “I” statements, nonverbal communication, healthy versus unhealthy relationship patterns, sexual communication and consent, and common barriers to effective listening. The page includes specific examples and strategies couples can use to communicate more clearly and resolve conflicts more constructively.

21. Managing Conflict in Relationships: 3 Essential Blueprints for Couples – The Gottman Institute

The Gottman Institute’s Managing Conflict in Relationships guide offers three practical “conflict blueprints” for navigating disagreements as a couple. Drawing on relationship research, it covers managing current conflicts, healing past emotional injuries, and handling recurring problems that may never be completely resolved. The guide includes strategies for expressing needs respectfully, listening without interrupting, calming heated conversations, making repair attempts, taking responsibility, apologizing, and finding compromises that respect both partners’ needs.

22. Coping with Problems and Challenges – SMART Couples – University of Florida, Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences – UF/IFAS

The University of Florida’s SMART Couples program offers a collection of free resources for couples coping with relationship problems and challenges. Topics include constructive conflict, destructive communication patterns, mindfulness, and understanding why communication skills alone may not solve every relationship problem. The page also includes a downloadable guide with 10 rules couples can use to handle disagreements more constructively.

Advertisement
Privacy Settings

23. Resources for Couples – Healthy Marriage and Responsible Fatherhood

The National Healthy Marriage Resource Center offers a large collection of free resources designed to help couples strengthen their relationships and navigate common challenges. The library includes tip sheets on communication, active listening, trust, forgiveness, infidelity, financial stress, commitment, chronic illness, emotional cheating, and blended families. Couples can explore individual topics or use the collection to find practical strategies for communicating more effectively and working through problems together.

24. What Type of Communication during Conflict is Beneficial for Intimate Relationships? – PMC

This research review examines which types of communication actually help couples during conflict and finds that there may not be one approach that works in every situation. The authors explore constructive and destructive communication patterns, including cooperation, opposition, affection, validation, defensiveness, and direct versus indirect communication. The review offers a more nuanced look at how the effectiveness of different communication styles can depend on the couple and the problem they’re trying to solve.

Advertisement
Privacy Settings

25. Toolkit for Couples – Healthy Relationships Initiative

The Healthy Relationships Initiative’s Toolkit for Couples offers free resources designed to help couples build healthier, stronger relationships. The toolkit encourages partners to reflect on their relationship, have deeper conversations, strengthen their connection, and develop skills for navigating challenging areas together. It’s designed for couples at different stages, whether your relationship is generally going well, you’re struggling with particular issues, or you’re experiencing more serious difficulties. A free PDF version of the complete toolkit is available.
